Information received since February points to continued labor-market strength and moderate growth, with inflation close to the 2% objective. The FOMC’s 25 bp hike to a 0.75–1.00% target range, coupled with language that policy remains accommodative and increases will be gradual and data-dependent, is consistent with the inertial, rule-like policy behavior documented by Clarida, Galí, and Gertler and with flexible inflation targeting as in Svensson and Woodford. Operationally, the use of IOER at 1.00% and the ON RRP at 0.75% reflects the Goodfriend-style implementation framework that maintains control of short rates. Forward guidance that the funds rate will stay below its longer-run level for some time helps anchor expectations despite low market-based inflation compensation. Overall, this reads as a “dovish hike”: credible tightening within an accommodative, predictable framework.
